subject: AI & Agents
title: Word2Vec: Words Become Math
description: A micro-lesson that makes Word2Vec: Words Become Math usable.

hook.text: King minus Man plus Woman equals Queen. Words became vectors, and analogies became algebra.

buildup.text: In 2013, Mikolov at Google published Word2Vec — efficient word embeddings from vast text corpora.

discovery.text: Words with similar meanings clustered together in vector space automatically.

twist.text: The embeddings also captured societal biases — 'doctor' was closer to 'man' than 'woman.'

climax.text: Word2Vec became the foundation for nearly every NLP breakthrough that followed.

punchline.text: Turn words into numbers and language becomes computable.

quiz.question: What did Word2Vec demonstrate about word relationships?
options: Words with similar meanings cluster together as vectors
Every word gets a unique random number

details.summary: Word2Vec, introduced by Google in 2013, converted words into numerical vectors where meaning relationships became mathematical operations. The famous example: king minus man plus woman equals queen.
details.whyItMatters: Word2Vec showed that language has mathematical structure machines can exploit. It became the foundation for all modern language AI, from search engines to GPT-style models.
takeaways: Word2Vec represents words as numerical vectors in space
Meaning relationships become mathematical operations between vectors
It laid the groundwork for all modern language AI systems

faq.question: How does the king-queen example work?
faq.answer: In Word2Vec's vector space, subtracting the 'man' vector from 'king' and adding 'woman' produces a vector very close to 'queen.' The model learns that gender is a consistent directional relationship in the space.

faq.question: How did Word2Vec influence modern language AI?
faq.answer: It proved that representing words as dense vectors captures meaning. This concept evolved into contextual embeddings in models like BERT and GPT, which use the same fundamental idea at massive scale.
